links.outcome: Effect of retrieval augmentation on long-context medical QA comprehension across single- and multi-document datasets
links.effect: RAG excels in challenging cases and has best settings differing between single- and multi-document QA datasets, but shows limitations in cases requiring temporal reasoning. No numbers reported in the abstract.
links.quote: Our quantitative analysis reveals challenging cases where RAG excels while still showing limitations in cases requiring temporal reasoning.

unlisted_practices: Providing full long patient context versus truncated or relevant-only context to LLMs for medical QA
Using reasoning models over non-reasoning models for long-context medical QA

screen.reason: The paper empirically investigates the impact of adding Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) to LLMs across long-context medical question answering benchmarks.
